subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Oxides of nitrogen formed in car engines contribute to:
questions.explain: Oxides of nitrogen contribute to acid rain and cause respiratory problems.

questions.q: Why is cracking carried out on some crude oil fractions?
options: Demand for short-chain fractions like petrol is greater than supply
There is too little demand for short-chain hydrocarbons
questions.explain: Cracking matches supply to demand, as there is more demand for short-chain hydrocarbons than the supply from crude oil.

questions.q: What process caused the amount of oxygen in the atmosphere to increase?
questions.explain: Algae and plants increased oxygen levels through photosynthesis.

questions.q: What is the general formula of the alkanes?
questions.explain: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with the general formula CnH2n+2.

questions.q: The complete combustion of a hydrocarbon produces:
questions.explain: Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon produces carbon dioxide and water.

questions.q: Ethanol belongs to which homologous series?
questions.explain: Ethanol is a member of the alcohol homologous series.

questions.q: Carbon from the early atmosphere became locked away in which type of rock?
questions.explain: Carbon became locked in sedimentary rocks like limestone and in fossil fuels.

questions.q: Which property generally increases as the hydrocarbon chains in a fraction get longer?
questions.explain: Longer hydrocarbon molecules have higher boiling points and are more viscous.

questions.q: Cracking is used to convert long-chain hydrocarbons into:
options: Shorter, more useful molecules including alkenes
questions.explain: Cracking breaks long-chain hydrocarbons into shorter, more useful molecules, including alkenes.

questions.q: The first stage of treating fresh water to make it potable is usually:
questions.explain: Water is first filtered through filter beds to remove insoluble solids before sterilisation.

questions.q: What is the approximate composition of clean dry air today?
questions.explain: Today's air is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen, with small amounts of other gases.

questions.q: Which of these is a greenhouse gas?
questions.explain: Methane is a greenhouse gas, along with carbon dioxide and water vapour.

questions.q: Sulfur dioxide released from burning fuels causes which environmental problem?
questions.explain: Sulfur dioxide dissolves in rain water to form acid rain.

questions.q: In addition polymerisation, the monomers must contain:
questions.explain: Addition polymers form from monomers containing a C=C double bond, which opens up to join together.

questions.q: During incomplete combustion of a hydrocarbon, which products may form?
options: Carbon monoxide and/or carbon (soot), and water
questions.explain: Incomplete combustion in limited oxygen can produce carbon monoxide and/or carbon as well as water.

questions.q: Which human activity increases the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere?
questions.explain: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide, adding to atmospheric levels.

questions.q: Which of these is the main greenhouse gas released by burning fossil fuels?
questions.explain: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide, the main greenhouse gas from this activity.

questions.q: In a fractional distillation column, the temperature is:
options: Hottest at the bottom and cooler at the top
The same all the way up
questions.explain: The column is hottest at the bottom and gets cooler higher up, so fractions condense at different heights.

questions.q: Hydrocarbons are compounds containing only:
questions.explain: A hydrocarbon contains only the elements hydrogen and carbon.

questions.q: Particulates released from burning fuels can cause:
questions.explain: Particulates cause global dimming and can damage health by causing respiratory problems.

questions.q: What is the general formula of the alkenes?
questions.explain: Alkenes have the general formula CnH2n.

questions.q: Why are fossil fuels described as finite resources?
options: They form much faster than we use them
They are being used up faster than they form
questions.explain: Fossil fuels take millions of years to form, so they are finite and being used up faster than they are replaced.
